Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

with preposition

in company, together with

also with me, with you, with us, along with, together with

classical

Sen. Ep. 55.11: mēcum studē, mēcum cēnā, mēcum ambulā
Hor. Ep. 1.7.70: sī cēnās hodiē mēcum

cum + abl.

preposition with the ablative; written after the pronouns: mēcum, tēcum, sēcum, nōbīscum, vōbīscum

with, together with

Of the people one is with, and of things one has with one (cum clāvī, with the key). Not of a tool: “with a knife” is the plain ablative (see “with”, the tool). Of manner, magnā cum cūrā, though an adverb is often plainer (dīligenter).

Other words

  • ūnā cum + abl. — along with, together with

    adverb with the preposition cum · also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 556: ūnā tēcum bona mala tolerābimus; Traupman 270

    Stresses the being together; see together.

Examples

  • itaque mēcum studē, mēcum cēnā, mēcum ambulā

    so study with me, dine with me, walk with meSen. Ep. 55.11

  • sīc ignōvisse putātō mē tibi, sī cēnās hodiē mēcum. — ut libet

    consider yourself forgiven, if you dine with me today. — As you like.Hor. Ep. 1.7.69–70

  • Nōlī metuere: ūnā tēcum bona mala tolerābimus.

    Don’t be afraid: we’ll bear the good and the bad together with you.Ter. Ph. 556

  • venī ergō mēcum

    come with me, thenPhaedr. 3.7.15

  • fuistī here nōbīscum

    you were with us yesterdaySen. Ep. 64.1

  • jamdūdum in vīllā sedēns exspectō cum clāvī tē … — em quīn adsum, veniō ad līmen, forēs aperī

    I’ve been sitting in the house with the key waiting for you for ages … — Here I am, I’m coming to the door, open up!Varr. RR 1.56

See also together, with, without.
